column1: # 0x82211B40 and 0x82211988 -- the slot masks around the binding layer. Cycle 1357.
# `.pdata` has NO ROW for 0x82211B40; check_listing_against_pdata says so rather
# than guessing, so its 51 instructions are read without a length control.
# 0x82211B40 (r3 = player block, r4 = record base, r5 = the mask word) uses NO
# FLOATING-POINT INSTRUCTION AT ALL. It gathers a mask:
#   if [r4 + 0x08] == 0 -> return            THE RECORD'S FLAG WORD
#   loop until r11 - 2 >= 32:
# So it sets one bit per player-block mask word that INTERSECTS the record's flag
# word -- the same 32 mask words at player+0x08 that 0x82211C10 walks, and the
# same flag word `retail_input_record` already ports at record+0x08.
# 0x82211988 then reads the pair 0x82211DF8 set up and computes EDGES:
#   r9 = [this + 0xE44]      this frame's mask
#   r10 = [this + 0xE48]     last frame's, saved by 0x82211DF8
#   [this + 0xE4C] = r9 & ~r10           newly active
#   [this + 0xE50] = r10 & ~r9           newly inactive
# THAT IS THE SAME ALGEBRA `button_edges` ALREADY PORTS, one level up. retail_input
# computes (prev ^ cur) & cur and (prev ^ cur) & ~cur on device buttons; this
# computes cur & ~prev and prev & ~cur on SLOTS. The two forms are equal, and the
# second was read from a function that shares nothing with the first.
# columns: offset meaning
